purpose: Preserved original historical test-count paragraphs moved out of the main reading path in d4. They are dated observations with overlapping scopes, not additive current totals.

entries.text: For comparison with the archived checkpoint, CP03 originally recorded 46 passes: seven routing cases, fourteen workspace/protocol checks and twenty-five discovery tests. The current integrated report contains later chapters too. These counts describe software checks on synthetic inputs; user research is a separate activity.

The historical CP02 reference recorded seven Chapter~1 acceptance passes and fourteen new Chapter~2 tests, for \textbf{21 passing offline tests}; use the shared runner's current report for the integrated total. The new tests check instruction and skill structure, adapter projection into temporary repositories, the allowlisted code-edit path, protected-file hashes, negative paths and symlink behavior, and a minimal MCP stdio message exchange. The original output and interpreter version are captured in \texttt{reader\_side/evidence/CP02\_OFFLINE\_RESULTS.json}. Those results came from local Python execution. No paid coding assistant was used, and no claim of end-to-end MCP-host compatibility follows from this test run.

The historical CP04 suite reports \textbf{93 passes}: seven Chapter~1 acceptance tests, fourteen Chapter~2 workspace/MCP checks, twenty-five Chapter~3 discovery tests and forty-seven Chapter~4 specification tests. Use the shared runner's current report for the integrated total. The intentionally unsafe Chapter~4 starter produces \textbf{11 review issues}; the protected synthetic reference produces none. These are local executions of deterministic checks, not a score for any SDD product or LLM. The companion contains the logs, data fixtures, and case oracle.

The historical CP06 author checkpoint passed \textbf{179 offline tests}: seven original routing acceptance tests and 172 additional selected checks covering Chapters~1--6. The unsafe starter produced \textbf{24 findings}; the reference pair produced none. For current combined totals, use the integrated runner's report. No LLM was called in the checkpoint tests. They validate a teaching implementation and selected invariants; they cannot establish a safe autonomous tool runtime, an effective prompt-injection defense, or the truth of synthetic policy facts.

Use the current integrated run report for the combined Chapters~1--14 total. The CP09 integration gate described above remains the cumulative review of Chapters~1--9, including the direct Chapter~8 verification. Do not add historical checkpoint totals together: their inherited tests overlap. A reader should also be suspicious of any account that combines the historical 191 suite tests, eight contract examples and three mutant checks into a single percentage labelled \enquote{AI-generated software reliability}. They answer different questions and are not independent samples of one underlying population. We do not have a real user evaluation, a randomized agent comparison, production telemetry, a full security penetration test, or a statistical estimate of residual defects.
